chunks: namely: unreasonableness (contention), fear, wavering, and submission.
So, he who adopts unreasonableness as his way, for him there is no dawn after the night;
he who is afraid of what befalls him has to run on his heels;
ai.seo_question: What are the four aspects of doubt and their consequences according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Imam Ali categorizes doubt into four distinct spiritual states, linking each to a specific consequence: persistent argumentation (tamarrī) blinds the heart, overwhelming fear (hawl) causes regression, wavering (taraddud) invites the devils' trampling, and total submission to worldly ruin (istislam) ensures destruction in both worlds. This taxonomy reflects the Shia emphasis on the internal psychological state of the believer as the determinant of spiritual fate, moving beyond mere intellectual uncertainty to active spiritual conditions.
